records.review: Pinned LTS already rejects direct I/O for compressed files in f2fs_force_buffered_io, now in file.c. The entire current predicate equals LTS, including fscrypt/verity, inline-data, device-alignment, zoned-write and disabled-checkpoint checks. This repairs a historical merge error that is absent in the selected code; preserve native predicate to avoid bypassing compression decoding.

The original FSSETXATTR mask correction is upstream. Current LTS/native fileattr conversion computes masked_flags and compares only selected casefold/compression flags, retaining unselected inode flags. Later upstream compression eligibility/locking supersedes the old compression transitions. Current port adds only separately reviewed alias rejection and compression veto to that helper; project-quota validation and VFS fileattr permission checking are retained. Do not resurrect the obsolete unmasked BUG_ON.

Pinned LTS already implements the encryption-nonce helper and both native/compat ioctl dispatch. The helper is byte-identical in the port and checks the encryption feature before fscrypt_ioctl_get_nonce; the common helper validates context length/version and bounded copy_to_user. This is the nonce, not a key; preserve existing interface and errors.

The mask-before-update fix is upstream and retained: iflags &= mask replaces the historical BUG_ON, and masked_flags and final assignment preserve flags outside the request. VFS fileattr conversion shrinks the mask for xflags requests. This avoids incorrectly rejecting/bugging a legitimate flag operation while keeping quota, compression and casefold constraints.

The lazytime parser restoration is upstream; later native fs_context parsing represents lazytime/nolazytime with fsparam_flag_no and ctx_set_opt/ctx_clear_opt. The native mount applies LAZYTIME to SB_LAZYTIME and remount keeps the native flag propagation. Keep the current parser rather than replaying removed match_table/parse_options machinery. No change to native timestamp durability semantics.
